findings.title: Rewrapping `MissingPyprojectToml` as a string error breaks the caller's `uv self version` fallback.
findings.body: Before this change, `.await?` turned the `WorkspaceError` into an `anyhow::Error` that still held the original type. Now `MissingPyprojectToml` becomes a plain `anyhow!` string, so `err.downcast_ref::<WorkspaceError>()` can no longer find it. The test names `version_get_fallback_missing_strict` and `version_get_fallback_missing_strict_preview` suggest the caller uses that downcast to decide whether plain `uv version` falls back to printing uv's own version with a warning. If it does, a bare `uv version` outside a project now exits with an error instead of falling back. I could not see the caller, which is why confidence is medium. The same problem is in the copy at lines 362-371. Fix: keep the typed error here and add the hint only where the caller actually reports the error (the strict/`--project`/`--preview` path), or wrap it with `.context(...)` so `downcast_ref` still finds it.

findings.title: New test expects plain `uv version` to fail, which contradicts the non-strict fallback.
findings.body: `version_get_missing_with_hint` expects a bare `uv version` with no `pyproject.toml` to exit with code 2. The neighbouring `*_strict` / `*_strict_preview` tests suggest that only strict mode (`--project`/`--preview`) should fail, and that the normal mode falls back to `uv self version`. If so, this test either fails against the intended behaviour or locks in the fallback regression caused by the downcast change in `find_target`. The issue only asked for a hint, not for removing the fallback. Fix: restore the fallback and drop this test, or make it assert the fallback output.
